messages:
ben_dev: hitting a regression in production — our Python client getting 'Unexpected end of JSON input' when using JSON streaming mode. Started ~10:12 UTC. trace_id=trace-0x7b9f. Not all requests fail, looks like partials.

alice_support: thanks Ben — can you paste the minimal repro + SDK version? any logs from the server side? :mag:

ben_dev: python SDK 0.7.2, streaming=True, mode='json'. quick repro: 
```py
from redwood import RedwoodClient
cli = RedwoodClient(api_key=... , sdk_version='0.7.2')
resp = cli.generate_stream(model='rw/large', json=True)
for chunk in resp:
    obj = json.loads(chunk)  # fails here sometimes
    print(obj)
```
error: json.decoder.JSONDecodeError: Unterminated string starting at: line 1 column 134 (char 133)

ben_dev: raw chunk sequence (abridged):
```
data: {"json": {"answer": "Hello

I can help"}}\n\n```
data: {"json": {"answer": " with examples", "_meta": {"part": 2}}}\n```
The first chunk ends mid-string, second finishes it — but current client treats each 'data' chunk as a full JSON document.

dave_sdk: copying in — this is a bug in the python streaming parser in 0.7.2. We were calling json.loads on each SSE payload instead of buffering until a complete top-level object is available. The server emits JSON objects that can be split across SSE chunks. That explains the "Unexpected end".

carol_eng: is TS or Go seeing the same?

ben_dev: yes — TS 0.6.8 shows 'Unexpected token } in JSON at position 512' when model outputs trailing commas in generated structured sections. Go client (using json.Decoder) sometimes gets "invalid character '\\x00' after top-level value" when chunk boundaries include null-bytes from stream framing.

alice_support: short-term mitigation: set streaming=False or use 'json_mode': 'ndjson' in requests so server emits one JSON object per line. For python, as a workaround you can concatenate chunks and only call json.loads when braces are balanced. Not ideal but works.

dave_sdk: root cause summary: two defects — 1) python/ts clients assumed each SSE 'data:' line is a self-contained JSON doc; 2) server sometimes emitted structured output with trailing commas (model generation artifact) causing invalid JSON. We've got a fix for (1) which implements an incremental buffer + simple brace balance heuristic and proper SSE event concatenation. For (2) we added a post-processing sanitiser to close trailing commas to keep backward compatibility.

carol_eng: action plan (P1):
- dave: publish python 0.7.3 + ts 0.6.9 with streaming buffer fix and unit tests for split chunks.
- eng: server fallback to NDJSON header when negotiation fails for 48h.
- qa: add stress test with random chunking and trailing comma cases.
- support: notify customers with the trace prefix if they hit parse failures.

dave_sdk: PRs: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/pull/3456 and github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/pull/2789. Added header negotiation "X-Stream-Format: ndjson" and tests verifying balanced-brace buffer. Also added more robust SSE parsing for chunked payloads.

ben_dev: tested 0.7.3 locally — fixes the repro. will push canary to prod later today and confirm traces clear. thanks team. :pray:

deploy-bot: deploy started for sdk-python@0.7.3 and sdk-js@0.6.9 to pypi/npm at 14:05 UTC :rocket:

alice_support: marking ticket CS-9987 as 'monitoring' — close when you confirm traces gone by EOD. Reopen if anything else shows up.

ben_dev: confirmed after canary: 0 hits for trace-0x7b9f in last 30m. reopening if we see regressions. thanks everyone! :thumbsup:
